newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end firmer from retreat from record.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end firmer from retreat from record.

text.p: Swiss shares closed firmer on Wednesday but the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) backed off an all-time high of 4813.7 points after Wall Street opened weak.
Wall Street's second-biggest point jump in history on Tuesday, the firmer dollar, the stronger bond market and options related buying supported the market, dealers said.
The SMI ended up 28.8 points or 0.61 percent to 4,781.1 points.The broad Swiss Performance Index advanced 16.39 points, or 0.55 percent, at 3,022.83 points.
Dealers said demand came mainly from professional traders while retail investors stayed on the sidelines.
Option-related buying pushed prices higher as a flood of new warrants was issued during the day.
SBC set call warrants on Novartis and Swissair, and UBS brought calls on Swiss Re.
Volume leader Novartis added eight francs and closed at 1,884. One dealer said there was some switching from Novartis to Roche. Roche certificates ended 140 francs higher at 12,200 francs.
Nestle eased eight francs to 1,754 in active trade.
Alusuisse and Ems consolidated after Tuesday's price-pushing speculation that Ems could buy Alusuisse's Lonza division, one dealer said.
Alusuisse ended seven francs lower at 1,221 francs. Ems lost 10 francs and closed at 6,000.

Second-tier Keramik Laufen closed steady at 750 after reporting net profit for 1996 dropped to 30 million francs from 52 million in 1995. For 1997 the group expects to improve net profit considerably, a group spokesman said.
